chapters.1.summary: After Moses dies, the LORD tells Joshua to lead Israel across the Jordan. He promises to give them every place their feet tread. He says he will be with Joshua as he was with Moses. He tells Joshua three times to be strong and courageous. Joshua must keep the law and think on it day and night. Joshua tells the officers to prepare to cross in three days. He reminds Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh to fight beside their brothers. They promise to obey him as they obeyed Moses.
chapters.1.lds: The Church lesson connects courage with God’s presence and repeated scripture study. What is Joshua told to do with the book of the law (verse 8)?
chapters.2.summary: Joshua secretly sends two spies to Jericho. They stay in the house of Rahab, a prostitute. The king sends for them, and Rahab hides them under flax on her roof. She tells the king’s men that the spies already left. She tells the spies the LORD has given Israel the land. She asks them to spare her family, and they swear to it. She lets them down by a cord from her window in the city wall. She must tie a scarlet cord there and keep her family inside.
chapters.2.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Rahab as an example of faith expressed through action. What does Rahab say about the LORD in verse 11?
chapters.3.summary: Israel camps at the Jordan for three days. The officers tell the people to follow the ark at a distance. Joshua tells them to make themselves ready for the LORD’s wonders. The LORD says he will make Joshua great, as he was with Moses. The priests carry the ark to the river, which is in flood at harvest. When their feet touch the water, the river stops and piles up far upstream. The priests stand on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All Israel crosses over near Jericho.
chapters.3.lds: The Church lesson connects the crossing with trust in Christ and the promise of baptism. When does the water stop, according to verses 13 and 15?
chapters.4.summary: After the crossing, the LORD tells Joshua to choose twelve men, one from each tribe. Each carries a stone from the riverbed where the priests stood. Joshua also sets up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan. About forty thousand armed men cross toward Jericho. That day the people honor Joshua as they had honored Moses. When the priests come out, the river returns and overflows its banks. Israel camps at Gilgal, and Joshua sets up the twelve stones there. The stones are for children who will ask what they mean.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me asks readers to recognize God’s help and teach the next generation. What question will children ask about the stones (verse 6)?
chapters.5.summary: The kings of the land hear about the Jordan and lose heart. The LORD tells Joshua to circumcise the men born in the wilderness. The older generation had died there for not listening. The LORD says he has rolled away Egypt’s reproach, and the place is named Gilgal. Israel keeps the Passover in the plains of Jericho. They eat the produce of the land, and the manna stops. Near Jericho Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword. He is commander of the LORD’s army, and Joshua bows and removes his sandals.
chapters.5.lds: The older manual proposes that the commander may be the Lord. It acknowledges the limited details. Joshua asks whose side the man is on (verse 13). How does the man answer in verse 14?
chapters.6.summary: Jericho is shut tight. The LORD tells Joshua to march around it once a day for six days. Seven priests carry ram’s horn trumpets before the ark. On day seven they circle seven times and shout, and the wall falls flat. Israel destroys everyone in the city, young and old, and the animals. The two spies bring out Rahab and her whole family. The city is burned, and its metals go to the LORD’s treasury. Rahab lives in Israel from then on, and Joshua curses anyone who rebuilds Jericho.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies trust and obedience through the account of Jericho. Why was Rahab saved, according to verse 25?
chapters.7.summary: Achan of Judah secretly takes some of the goods devoted to the LORD. Israel sends about three thousand men against Ai, and they are driven back. Thirty-six die, and the people lose heart. Joshua falls before the ark and asks why God brought them over the Jordan. The LORD says Israel has sinned and stolen devoted things. The next morning Judah is singled out, then a family, then Achan. Achan confesses that he hid a robe, silver, and gold under his tent. Israel stones him and his household in the valley of Achor.
chapters.7.lds: Come, Follow Me studies how Achan’s hidden choice harms other people. What steps does his confession name in verse 21?
chapters.8.summary: The LORD tells Joshua not to fear and to set an ambush behind Ai. Joshua hides men west of the city and camps the rest to the north. Israel pretends to flee, and every man of Ai chases them. Joshua stretches out his javelin, and the hidden men take and burn the city. Twelve thousand people of Ai die, and its king is hanged. Israel keeps the livestock and goods this time. Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and writes the law on stones. He reads every word to all Israel, with the women, children, and foreigners.
chapters.8.lds: The manual connects the public reading with Moses’s instructions. Who is named among the hearers in verse 35?
chapters.9.summary: The kings west of the Jordan join to fight Israel. The people of Gibeon choose a trick. They come with worn sacks, patched sandals, and moldy bread, and claim a far country. Israel’s men taste their food and do not ask the LORD. Joshua makes a covenant to let them live, and the leaders swear to it. Three days later Israel learns that they live nearby. The people grumble, but the leaders will not break an oath sworn by the LORD. The Gibeonites become woodcutters and water carriers for the altar.
chapters.9.lds: The older Church manual studies keeping a promise when its cost becomes clear. What did Israel’s men fail to do in verse 14?
chapters.10.summary: Five Amorite kings, led by Jerusalem’s king, attack Gibeon for making peace with Israel. Gibeon begs Joshua not to abandon it. Joshua marches all night from Gilgal and surprises them. The LORD throws them into confusion and sends great hailstones. Joshua asks for the sun and moon to stand still, and they do. The five kings hide in a cave at Makkedah and are later put to death. Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir. He holds the southern land because the LORD fought for Israel.
chapters.10.lds: The older Church manual compares the long day with Helaman 12. Gibeon asks Joshua not to abandon it (verse 6). How does Joshua respond in verses 7–9?
chapters.11.summary: Jabin king of Hazor gathers the northern kings with horses and chariots. Their army is like the sand of the seashore. The LORD tells Joshua not to fear. Joshua attacks suddenly at the waters of Merom and wins. He cripples their horses and burns their chariots, as the LORD said. He burns Hazor, the leading city, but not the other cities on their mounds. The war with these kings lasts a long time. Joshua takes the whole land, and the land rests from war.
chapters.11.lds: How does Joshua respond to God’s instructions before the battle (verses 6 and 9)? What does verse 18 say about how long the war took?
chapters.12.summary: This chapter lists the kings Israel defeated. East of the Jordan, Moses defeated Sihon of Heshbon and Og of Bashan. Their land went to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. West of the Jordan, Joshua defeated kings from the hill country to the lowland. The list names each city’s king and counts “one” after each. It begins with Jericho and Ai. It includes Jerusalem, Hebron, Lachish, Hazor, and Megiddo. The total is thirty-one kings.
chapters.12.lds: Why does the list include victories on both sides of the Jordan? Who led each set of battles (verses 6–7)?
chapters.13.summary: Joshua is old, and the LORD says much land remains to be taken. The Philistine regions, the Geshurites, and lands toward Lebanon are still unconquered. The LORD promises to drive those peoples out. Joshua must divide the western land among nine and a half tribes. The chapter then reviews the eastern land Moses gave. Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh each receive their towns there. Israel did not drive out the Geshurites and Maacathites. Levi receives no land, because the LORD is their inheritance.
chapters.13.lds: What duties remain after a tribe receives its share of land? What does the LORD say to Joshua in verse 1?
chapters.14.summary: Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal heads divide Canaan by lot. Caleb of Judah comes to Joshua at Gilgal. He recalls spying out the land at age forty and giving an honest report. Moses swore that the land he walked on would be his. Caleb is now eighty-five and says he is as strong as ever. He asks for the hill country where the Anakim live in walled cities. Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron. Then the land rests from war.
chapters.14.lds: The older Church manual connects Caleb’s faith with his request for an inheritance. What kind of land does Caleb ask for in verse 12?
chapters.15.summary: Judah’s land is described by its borders, from the Salt Sea to the Great Sea. Caleb receives Hebron and drives out three sons of Anak. He offers his daughter Achsah to whoever takes Debir. Othniel takes the city and marries her. Achsah asks her father for springs of water to go with her dry land. Caleb gives her the upper and lower springs. Judah’s towns are then listed by region. Judah could not drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.
chapters.15.lds: The manual studies land distribution. Achsah’s land is in the dry South (verse 19). What does she ask her father to add?
chapters.16.summary: The lot for Joseph’s sons starts at the Jordan near Jericho. It runs through Bethel toward Beth Horon and ends at the sea. Manasseh and Ephraim take their inheritance. Ephraim’s border is traced from Ataroth to the brook of Kanah. Ephraim also has towns set inside Manasseh’s land. They did not drive out the Canaanites of Gezer. Those Canaanites live among Ephraim and do forced labor.
chapters.16.lds: How does forced labor affect the Canaanites who remain? What two things does verse 10 say about Gezer?
chapters.17.summary: Manasseh, Joseph’s firstborn, receives land on both sides of the Jordan. Zelophehad’s five daughters come to Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders. They say the LORD commanded Moses to give them an inheritance. They receive land among their father’s brothers. Manasseh could not drive out the Canaanites and later forced them to work. Joseph’s people complain that one share is too small. Joshua tells them to clear the forest in the hill country. He says they can drive out the Canaanites despite their iron chariots.
chapters.17.lds: The manual studies the division of land. How do Zelophehad’s daughters state their claim in verse 4?
chapters.18.summary: All Israel gathers at Shiloh and sets up the Tent of Meeting. Seven tribes still have no land. Joshua asks how long they will put off taking it. Three men from each tribe walk the land and write it up in seven parts. Joshua casts lots for them before the LORD at Shiloh. The first lot is Benjamin’s, between Judah and Joseph. Its borders and towns are listed. Its towns include Jericho, Bethel, Gibeon, and Jerusalem.
chapters.18.lds: What helps the tribes share the land? What does Joshua send the men to do in verse 8?
chapters.19.summary: Simeon’s share lies inside Judah’s, because Judah’s part was too large. Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali receive their borders and towns. Dan’s share is listed last. Dan’s people also go north and take the town of Leshem. When all the tribes have land, Israel gives Joshua a share. He asks for Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He builds up the town and lives there. The division is finished at Shiloh, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.19.lds: The manual studies the division of land. When does Joshua receive his own land (verse 49)?
chapters.20.summary: The LORD tells Joshua to set up the cities of refuge. A person who kills by accident may flee to one. He states his case to the elders at the city gate. They take him in and give him a place to live. They must not hand him over to the avenger of blood. He stays until he stands trial and until the high priest dies. Three cities are west of the Jordan: Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron. Three are east: Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan.
chapters.20.lds: The manual explains refuge within the inherited legal system. Why may the elders not hand the man over (verse 5)?
chapters.21.summary: The Levite leaders come to Eleazar and Joshua at Shiloh. They recall that the LORD commanded towns and pasture for them. Each tribe gives towns from its own land. Aaron’s family receives thirteen towns in Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. The other Kohathites, the Gershonites, and the Merarites receive theirs by lot. In all the Levites receive forty-eight towns with pasture. The LORD gives Israel the land and rest on every side. Not one good promise of the LORD has failed.
chapters.21.lds: The manual connects these towns with support for Levites. Who gives the towns in verse 3?
chapters.22.summary: Joshua thanks Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh and sends them home. Near the Jordan they build a large altar. The other tribes hear of it and gather at Shiloh for war. First they send Phinehas and ten leaders to ask what it means. They fear another sin like Peor or Achan’s. The eastern tribes say the altar is not for sacrifice. It is a witness that their children also belong to the LORD. Phinehas is satisfied, and the war is called off.
chapters.22.lds: The manual studies the altar’s purpose. What did the western tribes do before going to war (verses 13–16)?
chapters.23.summary: Years later Joshua is old and calls Israel’s leaders together. He reminds them that the LORD fought for them. Nations still remain in the land, and the LORD will drive them out. Israel must keep the law of Moses and hold fast to the LORD. They must not serve the gods of those nations or marry among them. If they do, the LORD will stop driving the nations out. Those nations will become a snare, a whip, and thorns. As every good promise came true, so will the warnings.
chapters.23.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Joshua’s final counsel and choosing to remain faithful to God. What does verse 13 say the remaining nations would become?
chapters.24.summary: Joshua gathers all the tribes at Shechem. He speaks for the LORD and retells the story from Abraham to the conquest. Their fathers served other gods beyond the River. The LORD brought them from Egypt and gave them land they did not work. Joshua tells them to choose whom they will serve. He says he and his house will serve the LORD. The people promise three times, and Joshua sets up a stone as a witness. Joshua dies at 110, and Joseph’s bones are buried at Shechem.
chapters.24.lds: Come, Follow Me studies a deliberate choice to serve God. What does Joshua tell the people to put away (verses 14 and 23)?
